original_card.question: Does one changed supplier have complete source-bound native, caller, ordinary and outer admission coverage?
methods: Construct and independently check one source-bound instance of the stated first experiment.
Seek an exact counterexample or target-specific complete-budget obstruction to that same proposed change.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Pin the current sources and one obligation; the historical owner audit is an example, not evidence of a current bug.

first_step.inspect: Read revision 8, the selected review and live exact-source handoffs. Then follow this card's bounded first_experiment.
first_step.scope: Source-bound orientation only, not a supplier replay or theorem proof.

original_card.first_experiment: Choose one latest uncovered candidate and build a delta coverage map against the selected review. For P104, #5717 changes owned-lifetime assumptions and #5719 covers exact #5713 causal premises; neither automatically transfers to #5718. For BIT, #5679/#5708 need component admission and compatible outer use. Check controls and exact source identity before reuse; stop with one resolved gap or explicit remaining obligation. A heavy full replay requires a separate serial resource budget.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Judge the actual current supplier contract and complete signed target/paid bill; frozen-profile ceilings require an applicability proof.
allowed_variations: One exact source head, helper/cut region or quantified proposition and changed hypothesis; check live handoffs first. Different seeds are not different scopes.
scope_change_triggers: Changing source head, helper/cut domain, operation alphabet or caller boundary without recording the new scope.
Treating an archived proposal or local numerical pass as complete supplier admission.

actual_scope: Findings and objects for the Whitehead (t = -1, d = 0) hosted native on P104: (1) one hosted word on the #6936 mixed word with the outer Whitehead stage on the 8 hosted ports, its native, joint caller and invoice, replayed (kappa .0035927413806393823240, -0.9451% against #6936); (2) a helper-free d = 0 native on all 104 ports, replayed by two exact engines and 100 mutants; (3) the connected rho = 1 all-Whitehead root with 18 stages; (4) the exact price targets (break-even per port-call, replacement budget formula, pass line) and the routes closed and open against them. No kappa claim above #6936.
scope_change_reason: The card asks whether one changed supplier has complete native, caller, ordinary and outer coverage. This package covers the native, root and caller of a t = -1 supplier that is priced below the baseline, so it is not a candidate and makes no admission claim. It records the objects, the exact targets a better supplier must meet, and which routes are closed with their scope. Ordinary-call and outer admission of the hosted Whitehead word are quoted from its build record and are not replayed here.
bottleneck_link: Judge the actual current supplier contract and complete signed target/paid bill: the Whitehead stage saves public D on the hosts, and the owned rank-1 carriers it needs are the whole bill; both sides are priced exactly against #6936.
stop_rule: No kappa claim and no candidate. Stop when the objects and targets are recorded with their scope. A route is closed here only with the family, hypotheses and escapes stated; the open routes are listed with the first exact step each needs.
evidence: README.md and PROOF.md (objects, targets, closed and open routes, scope ledger); check.py (about 100 s: sha256 of every object, exact replay of both natives, both Whitehead roots with controls, exact kappa and invoice move, target arithmetic, the 104-port native with 100 mutants) and checks/check_joint_w.py (about 100 s: the single 78-role joint caller replayed mod p at four characters with controls, the invoice rebuilt from the roots); data/ with OBJECTS.json.

open_questions.question: Is there a d = 0 native at t = -1 whose owned mass is at most 1.66 per port per W call on P104 (1.69 at rho = 1 with 18 calls), with a public layer no dearer than the helper-free one (1652.63 R0)?
open_questions.why_it_matters: That is the pass line from the replacement budget. The windowed native here is exact and helper-free but pays 2.0 owned per port, over by 35.2 / 32.1 R0 per call; below the line the rho = 1 root's free-native ceiling is +19.33% and the outer root's +1.54% (+11.17% at w = 8).
open_questions.first_step: Build the Gamma coupling on the Y registers after the bounce on a 16 to 32 port toy, with the owned landings placed before the mixing, and report rank(beta I - gamma G Sigma) against the clique floor of 8.
open_questions.blocked_by: Not built: no frame-legal Y-to-Y network is known, and the read cost of its dense row space is unpriced.

open_questions.question: Can one owned run serve the beta crossings of many ports (Lemma M floor: 1 per port), so that the 208 owned moves of the windowed native drop by at least 35?
open_questions.why_it_matters: A shared crossing run is the only owned-mass route that keeps the free d = 0 window swap; a pass needs the saving at both outer and rho = 1 prices.
open_questions.first_step: Write the landing as exact rows for one dot-0 block and check whether the sum it carries leaves junk in the other ports' pre-swap X registers.
open_questions.blocked_by: A shared run carries the sum of the x's of its ports; whether the junk can be cancelled inside the frame law is open.

open_questions.question: Can a hybrid public layer give the beta crossing cheaply through Gram-type coupling (0.54 owned per port in the Gram-based layer) while a window swap still removes y?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The windowed native pays 2.0 owned per port and the Gram-based layer 1.54 with a mandatory 104 owned UP; a hybrid needs at most 172.8 / 175.9 owned per call to pass.
open_questions.first_step: Compute exactly W' = beta I - T[Y,X] for the chosen public schedule and its rank before any owned run.
open_questions.blocked_by: The swap needs the pre-content of Y_t to be disposable while Gram coupling lives in Y; no schedule reconciles both.
